sam_support: Hey team — I'm seeing intermittent SSE handshake failures for request id 0x7a3b9c in prod-us-east. Can someone attach a minimal curl reproducer and the engine debug bundle (trace id + server logs)? Need to reproduce locally before escalating to runtime.
ashley_se: Quick summary of what I saw: client gets 200 then stream closes after ~3s. No obvious 5xx. I tried a couple of variations, here's the minimal curl I used (redacted token):

```bash
curl -N -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-rw-3'
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream'
  -H 'X-Request-Id: 0x7a3b9c'
  --http2
```

sam_support: Perfect start. Two quick asks:
1) please re-run with `--no-buffer -i --raw --trace-ascii curl.trace` and attach curl.trace (do not paste unredacted secrets).
2) include the redwood engine logs for the time window + the trace.json from /var/lib/redwood/traces (redact Authorization values). The curl -i will show whether the server is sending a FIN or if the client sees a RST_STREAM.

james_infra: Also capture a short pcap while repro-ing — tcpdump on host outside the proxy (if possible):

sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/stream_0x7a3b9c.pcap -s 0 port 443 and host <client-ip> & sleep 30; pkill -f tcpdump

That helps us see whether proxy is closing the connection mid-chunk.

eli_eng: If you suspect chunked frame truncation, capture raw HTTP/2 frames from curl trace. If the trace shows `RST_STREAM` from remote side, include the server connection id. Example server log lines we want (paste around the event):

[2026-02-20T15:02:13Z] request_id=0x7a3b9c conn_id=42 accept="text/event-stream" handshake=TLSv1.3
[2026-02-20T15:02:14Z] request_id=0x7a3b9c ev=stream_open status=200 stream_state=open
[2026-02-20T15:02:17Z] request_id=0x7a3b9c ev=socket_closed reason=RST_STREAM code=1 remote_addr=10.2.4.8

ashley_se: Adding a short paste of the server logs we pulled (redacted tokens):

[2026-02-20T15:02:13Z] request_id=0x7a3b9c conn_id=42 accept=text/event-stream proto=h2 remote=10.2.4.8
[2026-02-20T15:02:14Z] request_id=0x7a3b9c ev=stream_start status=200 handler=stream-handler
[2026-02-20T15:02:16Z] request_id=0x7a3b9c ev=send_chunk size=1024
[2026-02-20T15:02:17Z] request_id=0x7a3b9c ev=socket_error code=RST_STREAM details="stream aborted by peer"

sam_support: This is useful. One more small validation: try forcing HTTP/1.1 to see if the issue is HTTP/2-specific (some proxies rewrite connection semantics). Command:

curl -N -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-rw-3'
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream'
  -H 'X-Request-Id: 0x7a3b9c'
  --http1.1 --no-buffer -i

If the stream stays open under http1.1, that strongly hints at intermediate HTTP/2 proxy issues.

ashley_se: FYI, when I re-ran with --http1.1 and bypassed our edge proxy, the stream stayed open for >60s. With the proxy enabled + http2 the behavior reproduces consistently.

eli_eng: Good repro path. For the debug bundle please include:
- curl.trace (from --trace-ascii)
- engine.log (10s before/after window)
- trace.json (if available)
- /etc/hosts and proxy config (if repro from an internal host)

Also include the exact curl command you used (copy/paste) and the raw -i response headers. We will run the same command from an isolated repro runner.

oncall-bot: @sam_support assigned incident INC-2026-112 to eng-runtime. Priority: P2.

sam_support: Thanks @ashley_se — once you upload the bundle to the ticket (INC-2026-112) ping me here and i'll kick off a repro in our lab with tcpdump + proxy shim. :thumbsup:

ashley_se: Will do. Quick troubleshooting note for others: forcing `Connection: keep-alive` in the header didn't help when the proxy strips/rewrites it. The only reliable workaround we found was bypassing the proxy or falling back to http1.1. Sharing bundle shortly. :white_check_mark:
